stories.stat_label: years old, the oldest wing-walker ever
stories.headline: At 99, she became the world's oldest wing-walker
stories.summary: Retired nurse Helga Duffy was strapped to the top of a small plane and flew for over 5 minutes, about 1,000 m up. Guinness confirmed the record, 3 months after a 97-year-old set it.
stories.why: Her niece saw the last record on the news and thought: Helga could do that.

stories.stat_label: years old, and built it alone
stories.headline: A 17-year-old built an app that works when phone networks die
stories.summary: After the 2023 earthquakes cut phone service, Emirhan Duman built Crisis Connect: phones pass messages to each other over Bluetooth, hopping from device to device. It's free and open source.
stories.why: The phones survived the quake; the towers didn't. His app uses what's left.

stories.stat_label: chickens was all she asked for
stories.headline: An orphaned bride asked for 2 chickens. A whole country came
stories.summary: A week before her wedding, Shahrazad said all she needed was 2 chickens for the meal. Algerians sent furniture, food and a gold jewellery set, and one donor pledged a monthly allowance.
stories.why: Locals even held a motorcycle parade so she'd know she wasn't alone.

stories.headline: A prairie herd passed 1,000 free-roaming bison for the 1st time
stories.summary: American Prairie's annual calf count put its herd at 1,016, the 1st time it has topped 1,000. The group hopes to reach 5,000 bison as it stitches together a giant reserve in Montana.
stories.why: The land could one day hold tens of thousands of wild bison.

fun_fact: Wing-walking began in the 1920s, when barnstorming pilots toured towns doing stunts on biplanes.
